Your answer above stands. Do only what the items below ask, then end with a short note of what you did. Do not repeat your answer. Write a closing block again only if the one above would now be wrong: an item faults it, or you must close `RUNNING` / `DO NOT CLEAR` (to keep a deferral, or because what you just started, such as a review, would die on a clear).

[prawduct v<VERSION> · gate: reflection]
REFLECTION: This session changed judgeable code and .prawduct/.session-reflected
  does not yet carry a reflection's two lines. Missing:
    - what you expected vs. what actually happened (the words "expected" and "actual")
    - the root cause when something went wrong, or "no defect" when nothing did
  Append them — a couple of sentences is enough. The narrative around them is
  yours: what changed, what surprised you, what the methodology helped or hindered.
  Reflect at work boundaries (after a Critic pass, a bug fix, an error recovery) and
  this gate never fires at /clear.

  If this session produced a durable lesson (a rule future sessions should follow),
  also add it to the area file under .claude/rules/learnings/ whose `paths:` cover it (or .claude/rules/learnings/core.md if every session needs it) as ONE line — the rules gate
  names any line over the limit. Learnings are one-line standing rules; the
  session reflection is the story behind them.

  Escape hatch: a gate above that genuinely cannot be satisfied this session
  can be waived with a specific reason. Drop the key of any gate you can satisfy:
    echo '{"reflection": "reason — be specific"}' > .prawduct/.gates-waived
  Empty reasons are rejected; the file clears at the next session boundary
  (a fresh start or /clear), so it outlives a resume/compact/fork. When waiving
  is appropriate: `/prawduct:methodology building` (Gate waivers).
